classifications.label: Environmental noise: temperature, air pressure, humidity, vibration.
Instrumental drift or calibration artifact: the 'beats' unit or measurement chain is drifting slowly, producing apparent variation that is not physical.
Operator or procedural variability: timing method, release angle, or trial protocol introduces human or procedural scatter.
Real geophysical or settlement-scale transient: local gravity anomaly, structural vibration from settlement machinery, or transient magnetic/electrostatic field coupling to apparatus.
Different physical setup or measurement protocol between lab and obs systems
Environmental variables (temperature, pressure, humidity, vibration) affect both systems but produce different effective scatter because they scale differently with apparatus geometry
Instrumental drift or uncharacterized calibration artifacts in one or both measurement chains
Operator or procedural variability (release angle, timing method, environmental recording) introduces scatter differently between systems
Real geophysical or settlement-scale transient (gravity anomaly, structural vibration, electromagnetic coupling) correlates differently with the two measurement locations or sensing methods

pendulum_lab and pendulum_obs measure different physical apparatus, or use fundamentally different measurement protocols (timing definition, counting method, apparatus geometry, pivot design, or sensor type).

Environmental variables (temperature, pressure, humidity, vibration) affect both systems with different scaling factors because apparatus geometry, thermal mass, location, or sensing methods differ; lack of correlation arises from decorrelated environmental forcing or out-of-phase response.

Uncharacterized calibration artifacts, systematic offsets, or timing-chain errors in one or both measurement systems; neither system validated against an independent physical standard (tuning fork, atomic clock, theory prediction, or external observer).

Operator or procedural variability: release angle, counting method, environmental recording, observer identity, or timing discipline differ between lab and obs runs, or changed partway through (e.g., day 11+ protocol shift).

Real geophysical or settlement-scale transient (gravity anomaly, structural vibration, electromagnetic coupling) correlates differently with the two systems because of location or sensing method differences.

pendulum_lab and pendulum_obs measure fundamentally different apparatus, protocols, or definitions of 'beat' (different pendulum length, pivot design, timing window, sensor type, or counting method); the baseline gap for pendulum_obs reflects deliberate protocol separation, not oversight.

Environmental variables (temperature, humidity, pressure, vibration, settlement disturbances) affect the two systems with different scaling factors due to different apparatus geometry, location, thermal mass, or sensor response; lack of correlation reflects spatial/temporal decorrelation or out-of-phase environmental forcing.

Uncharacterized calibration artifacts, systematic offsets, or timing-chain errors (clock calibration drift, sensor hysteresis, counting-method discretization, or timing-window definition) in one or both systems; neither has been validated against an independent physical standard.

Operator or procedural variability (release angle, counting method, observer identity, timing discipline, environmental recording) changed partway through the measurement campaign or differs between the two systems; e.g., a protocol change on day 11 or day 17.

Real geophysical or settlement-scale transient (gravity anomaly, seismic event, structural vibration, electromagnetic coupling to settlement power/machinery) correlates differently with the two systems because of location or sensing method; level change in pendulum_obs day 17 reflects a genuine geophysical event.
